speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources since the start of circuit breaker measures (a) how many stallholders operating in hawker centres managed by NEA and NEA-appointed operators have closed their hawker stalls due to a drop in business; (b) how many hawkers have embraced food delivery options and applied for Enterprise Singapore's Food Delivery Booster Package and NEA's one-off $500 funding; and (c) what are the reasons cited by hawkers for not using the food delivery platforms despite the grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Some stallholders, particularly those in the Central Business District, have chosen not to operate their stalls as the office crowd has thinned and business has fallen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Others like older stallholders have also temporarily closed their stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We have earlier announced our support for hawkers with three months of rental waivers as well as one month of subsidies to defray table-cleaning and centralised dishwashing costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will further to support hawkers to ensure that they need not pay for these services during the extended circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Food delivery services can help to open up a new revenue stream for hawkers, especially during this circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While the demand for food delivery services has generally increased during this period, there are hawkers who remain hesitant in subscribing to such services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Some may not be aware of the various options available or find the commission costs charged by more popular platforms prohibitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Others may be unfamiliar with and resistant to adopting new technology solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA and Enterprise Singapore or ESG, have launched initiatives to support hawkers in adopting food delivery services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA also introduced a one-time funding assistance of $500 for hawkers who adopt food delivery services and has been reaching out to hawkers to encourage adoption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will encourage more hawkers to make full use of this funding to set up an additional revenue stream, especially during this challenging period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Over the longer term, we recognise that the model for food delivery services, including the commission structures, would need to evolve if they are to be attractive to hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These models must strike a balance among all parties in the food delivery services eco-system, including hawker, delivery person and platform operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We are heartened that ground-up initiatives such as Hawkers United and SG Dabao have emerged in recent weeks – these help hawkers to advertise their food for delivery or pick-up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: There are also smaller operators with newer models that allow users to aggregate orders within a hawker centre and do not impose direct commissions on the hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: I encourage other established companies to review their business models to see how hawker food delivery can be a complementary and integral part of their broader suite of services.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our hawkers have been struggling to survive since the implication of the circuit breaker measures.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is especially true for hawkers who do not have the profit margins to adopt food delivery platforms.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many are trying every means they can think of, such as relying on Facebook groups to promote their stalls like the Hawkers United group, which the Senior Minister of State mentioned.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They have since garnered over 250,000 Facebook users.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While this and the various other ground-up initiatives might sound rudimentary, they are a sign that more help needs to be provided to our hawkers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I applaud the move by NEA and ESG to provide grants to help our hawkers manage the business costs of food delivery orders, could the Government do more to support the various ground-up initiatives by our hawkers?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second question is, with social distancing measures likely to continue even after the circuit breaker period has ended, I would like to ask if the Ministry has any medium to long-term plans to help our hawkers, particularly those who are unable to sign up with the food delivery platforms to adapt and survive, post-circuit breaker.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: About an hour ago, I just participated in the Tekka Online Market.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The process itself was quite smooth and I think the hawkers, the food stall holders are also trying to adapt.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps, the Government can help to structure such a framework to help our hawkers as well.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are actually working very closely with the Hawkers' Associations to encourage the hawkers to come on board.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And some of these operators do not impose a direct commission on the hawker food prices.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will put them up on an information package, including some of these portals like Hawkers United and SG Dabao, so that our hawkers have a good idea of the types of platforms available which they can adopt.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Once they have decided on one, the relevant companies will come on board to help them adopt these services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we are also looking at the longer term.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will be working with the food delivery companies – in fact, we are already engaging them – to see how they can adapt their model for the hawker centre context, with potentially lower costs for the hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is not just for the circuit breaker period but beyond.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, in recent years as well as just this year, we have got various programmes to support and sustain the hawker trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, this is not just about the circuit breaker but actually, how to help them to remain competitive in this very tough F&B environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That includes, for instance, a Hawkers' Development Programme where we have worked with Skillsfuture.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The hawkers can get onto modules to learn how to market themselves as well as leverage on social media, digitalisation, e-payment and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We encourage the hawkers to make use of this opportunity to upskill themselves and further develop their business.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Above all, I would like to encourage all Singaporeans to support our hawkers by patronising them, utilising food delivery services and takeaway, now.
